title: EU-LAC High-Level Event on Human Development and Health 2024 Summary Report
executive_summary: The EU-LAC High-Level Event on Human Development and Health held in Brussels (March 21-22, 2024) focused on enhancing collaboration for inclusive human development and equitable health access. Key discussions addressed universal access to affordable medicines, regulatory harmonization, and inclusive social policies targeting poverty, gender, and youth employment. The event launched the Team Europe Initiative "Inclusive and Equitable Societies in LAC," aligned with the SDGs. High-level participants included PAHO officials, EU Commission staff, and health authorities from Latin America and the Caribbean. Outcomes featured a EUR268 million EU funding commitment to support social services in LAC, aiming to mobilize up to EUR1 billion in investments, and the launch of the 'Regulators of the Americas Learning Pathway' training program. The event aligned with the EU’s Global Gateway Investment Agenda, targeting EUR45 billion mobilization for LAC by 2027, reinforcing EU-LAC partnership for sustainable and inclusive development.

Alignment of the event and initiatives with the EU's Global Gateway Investment Agenda targeting EUR45 billion mobilization for LAC by 2027.

top_actors.name: European Commission
top_actors.justification: The European Commission is prominently mentioned as a key participant and funder, announcing EUR268 million in support and aligning the event with its Global Gateway Investment Agenda, demonstrating major influence on funding, initiatives, and policy frameworks.

top_actors.name: Pan American Health Organization (PAHO)
top_actors.justification: PAHO officials are highlighted as key participants and are linked to coverage and collaboration efforts, indicating a significant role in health-related discussions and regional cooperation on equitable access to health products.

top_actors.name: Governments
top_actors.justification: Governments of countries like Honduras and Costa Rica participated, representing national health authorities and stakeholders, essential for implementing policies and commitments discussed, though less prominently featured than the EU Commission and PAHO.

top_themes.name: Bi-regional Cooperation
top_themes.justification: The entire event centers on strengthening collaboration between the EU and LAC regions, making bi-regional cooperation the core theme. It is directly linked to the event's objectives, participant composition, and outcomes, including funding and initiatives that require joint efforts.

top_themes.name: Social Cohesion
top_themes.justification: Inclusive social policies aimed at reducing poverty and inequality, focusing on gender, youth, and employment, are a major discussion point and a key objective. The launch of the Team Europe Initiative also targets social cohesion aligned with SDGs.

top_themes.name: Multilateralism
top_themes.justification: The event involves multiple stakeholders including PAHO, EU Commission, and various countries, reflecting a multilateral approach. The alignment with the EU Global Gateway agenda and large-scale investment mobilization further emphasize multilateral cooperation.
